summary: Provision ephemeral permission sandbox for infra replay and audit runs
description:
Issue summary: Request to create a short-lived, least-privilege sandbox environment that allows the Infra team to replay a production audit run and validate billing/permission findings without granting permanent broad rights.

Impact: Audit replay must run against production-like resources (read-only) to validate IAM policies and recreate cost anomalies. Current options (full project access or ad-hoc manual exports) are risky and slow. This sandbox will reduce time-to-validate and avoid giving long-lived elevated access.

Background: Finance + Security requested a replay of a week-long production billing spike. Infra will need read-only listing and metric access across a subset of prod accounts in both AWS and GCP for ~48 hours. We prefer impersonation/service-account-based access that can be revoked automatically.

Requested scope:
- Timebox: 48 hours starting 2026-03-15 08:00 UTC (flexible by +24h).
- AWS: assume-role into a scoped read-only role in account redwood-prod-billing (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ScopedBillingReadOnly) limited to cost and CloudWatch read APIs.
- GCP: service account impersonation for projects redwood-prod-main and redwood-prod-billing (roles/viewer + monitoring.viewer), with no write permissions.
- No console-level full-admin or ability to create keys.
- Access must be logged to our audit sink and short-lived (automated revocation).

Deliverables:
1) Provision the ephemeral roles/service account proxies and update the JIT broker policy.
2) Provide a one-line command for Infra to acquire the temporary creds (gcloud/assume-role wrapper).
3) Verify logging to audit sink and record the grant in the access-tracking confluence page.

Priority rationale: Not blocking customer traffic but time-sensitive for compliance and cost investigation.
steps_to_reproduce: N/A - access provisioning request rather than a reproducible bug. See 'Requested scope' in description.
investigation_notes:
Initial checks: existing JIT broker supports both AWS STS assume-role and GCP service account impersonation. Current broker policy lacks the specific role ARNs for the two billing projects. Security reviewed and approved the read-only scope in principle (Slack thread #security-access 2026-03-09).
Hypotheses: 1) Easiest path is to add a new broker mapping for a short-lived 'audit-replay' profile. 2) Alternate is to create temporary service accounts in GCP with strict IAM conditions (e.g., time-bound condition).
Early findings: Ledger shows no prior ephemeral grants for this specific cross-cloud billing replay use-case; need explicit exceptions recorded. Linked INT-11456 contains a scoped debug role template we can adapt.

resolution: Pending - provisioning script staged in PR, waiting for final security signoff and schedule confirmation from Finance. Will close after a successful microphone replay and audit sink verification.
notes_for_engineers: If using GCP impersonation, prefer oauth2 service account impersonation with 1-hour tokens and IAM Conditions for timebound usage. For AWS, use sts:AssumeRole with an external ID and session duration capped at 1 hour. Ensure all assume/impersonation events are routed to the central audit sink and tagged with INT-25103.
